_provenance: HAND-AUTHORED FROM THE PINNED UPSTREAM SCHEMA. This is NOT a capture.
Transcribed from codex upstream tag rust-v0.151.0 — the exact version of the
binary this box spawns (~/.codex/packages/standalone/current/codex-package.json
-> 0.151.0). No codex turn was run to produce it: the only machine available
here is production, and #1255 forbids running real turns on it.
Shape: { threadId, turnId, explanation, plan: [{ step, status }] }.
`explanation` has no skip_serializing_if upstream, so treat it as optional AND
nullable.
DO NOT 'FIX' `inProgress` TO `in_progress`. The value below is camelCase
because the app-server wire is camelCase — the same frame spells `threadId`
and `turnId` that way.
Grepping the shipped binary settles nothing by itself, because BOTH spellings
are in it. Measured on this box's 0.151.0 binary (`grep -ao`; plain `grep -o`
returns nothing on a binary): `inProgress` 34 hits, `in_progress` 39,
`turn/plan/updated` 4. What the string table does show is which layer each
cluster belongs to: `in_progress` appears immediately beside `PlanItemArg` /
`UpdatePlanArgs` / `explanation` — the *core* `update_plan` tool-argument type,
which is snake_case — while `inProgress` appears inside the app-server type
cluster, adjacent to `struct PlanDeltaNotification` and its neighbours. Core
snake_case, app-server camelCase; this file transcribes the app-server frame.
A previous revision of this note claimed the binary contains ONLY the
snake_case spelling. That was false — it was asserted, not measured. The
`inProgress` value itself was always correct.
`threadId` here is a PLACEHOLDER and is not part of the transcription. The
kernel's `on_notification` prologue drops any notification whose `threadId` is
not the harness's current thread, so the test substitutes its own seeded id
(`SEED_THREAD_ID` in tests/cases/planner_harness_items_persist.rs) over this value
before emitting the frame. Changing the literal below changes nothing.
Once the kernel arm that persists these rows ships,
`SELECT params FROM harness_items WHERE method='turn/plan/updated'` promotes this
to a captured payload — and THAT, not this file, is what a UI slice gets built on.
